## Why it matters internationally

JRC Karlsruhe is the European Commission's main site for nuclear safety and
security research. Its Fuels and Materials Research laboratory offers radiance
spectroscopy of laser-heated samples to determine normal spectral emissivity in the
visible and near infrared above 1500 K, combining a 4.5 kW laser, a 256-channel
spectro-pyrometer and pressurised controlled atmospheres. The group has published
melting points and emissivities of nuclear and ultra-refractory materials such as
uranium and plutonium carbides, uranium nitrides and TaC–HfC, and took part in the
European metrology project Hi-TRACE on high-temperature thermophysical properties.

## Scope of activity

- **Quantities:** normal spectral emissivity of laser-heated solids and liquids (visible–near infrared) · radiance temperature and melting / solidification temperatures · thermal diffusivity at high temperature
- **Spectral range:** 515–980 nm (256-channel spectro-pyrometer); fast pyrometer at 655 nm
- **Temperature:** Spectral emissivity above 1500 K; laser-heating experiments beyond 3000 K
- **Methodology:** Samples heated by a 4.5 kW Nd:YAG laser in a pressurised controlled-atmosphere autoclave; temperature and normal spectral emissivity obtained together from a non-linear fit of the measured thermal-emission spectrum, with PTB-traceable lamp calibration.
- **Named facilities:** Laser heating with radiance spectroscopy (FMR laboratory) · CLASH thermal-diffusivity equipment (1200–3000 K)

**Application domains:** nuclear fuel safety and severe-accident research · melting behaviour of actinide oxides, carbides and nitrides · ultra-refractory ceramics and high-melting-temperature materials.

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- IR-EMPOWER 2026: Konstantinos Boboridis, “Benefits and Limitations of Multi-Wavelength Pyrometry”; scientific committee
- IR-EMPOWER 2024: Konstantinos Boboridis, “High melting temperature materials”; international advisory board
